summary: A satirical company policy note from Widget Wonders Inc. announcing "Operation Mind Mend," its Employee Mental Health Support and Counseling Services Policy. It lampoons corporate wellness through mandatory daily therapy, questionable therapists, group sessions, a soundproof booth, and compulsory off-site retreats, all framed as a way to keep resignation letters at bay.
one_line: Satirical Widget Wonders Inc. policy announcing Operation Mind Mend, a mandatory mental health program with daily therapy, group sessions, a scream booth and retreats.
key_facts: Widget Wonders Inc.'s motto is "Innovate. Elevate. Medicate."
The company's Employee Mental Health Support and Counseling Services Policy is branded "Operation Mind Mend."
Daily therapy sessions are mandated, with the jingle "A Therapy Session a Day Keeps the Resignation Letter Away."
Widget Wonders Inc. claims daily therapy can stave off spontaneous 'I quit' outbursts by at least 23%, with the disclaimer that the number is entirely fabricated.
The note says the company has spared moderate expense on its therapists and jokingly questions whether they are certified; they offer couches and sympathetic nodding for fifty minutes.
Group sessions turn the boardroom into a safe space where colleagues compare psychological scar tissue; admission requires only an employee badge.
The 'Just Bottle It Up' Booth is a soundproof booth where employees can scream between TPS report sessions.
Widget Wonders Inc. rolls out annual off-site retreats featuring 'trust fall' exercises and forced bonding with colleagues.
The note says the therapy happens during billable hours and lunch breaks, described as compulsory.
The introduction attributes the policy to endless hours, unrealistic deadlines, coffee that tastes like burnt popcorn, and companywide panic attacks.
